catalog_quote: 3.2.8 Stress. Stress, the relative degree of intensity with which the syllables of an Abu' word are spoken, is characterized in three different ways. An unmarked syllable has the weakest stress in the word, the strongest stress is marked with a " ´ ". Secondary (or intermediate) level of stress is marked by " ` ". Words of one syllable show no stress mark since there is no other stress level to which the syllable of monosyllabic words is compared. The following seems to be the pattern of rules governing stress. The first vowel of diphthong of bi- or poly-syllabic words receives primary stress (diphthongs override vowels). Once that is established, the secondary and the weakest stress is decided. audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the deciding passage is verbatim on thesis pp. 53-54 (PDF 67-68) of the Nekitel 1985 PDF we hold; locator and the 3.2.9 tone contrast are correct. (2) The deciding source is the only grammar-level description of Abu' (Glottolog's sole 'grammar', by a native-speaker linguist trained at ANU); no phonology article, JIPA illustration or instrumental study surfaced in Glottolog 5.1's bib, arapesh.org's bibliography, or OpenLibrary, and none is cited anywhere in the works opened. (3) The one open item not yet obtained, Nekitel 1986 (PL A-70), was downloaded and read: it gives 'Stress falls on the initial syllable' with rule /'V-/ and no diphthong clause, so it corroborates the initial-primary core of our the primary-stress rule and shows the CVV-override is specific to the (later, fuller, explicitly hedged) 1985 analysis; it does not warrant a reclassify of 'weight-hedged' (the hedge already captures this), but

sources.quote: p. 182: 'Vowels occurring in word-final positions are generally half-length. V -> V. / -#. Stress falls on the initial syllable. V -> V. / V-. Syllables may be open or closed. Neither stress nor tone appear to be phonemic in Abu'.' p. 183: 'Stress rule /'V - /kwafita/ ['kwafɩta] spoon, /dabah/ ['dabah] finger, /utam/ ['ʔutãm] stone. Neither stress nor tone are phonemic in Abu'.' No diphthong clause; the nasalisation list on the same page transcribes /noboil/ ['nõmboil] 'marsh' with initial stress despite /oi/ in the second syllable.
sources.locator: sec. 1.4.2.3 'Vowel length', p. 182; 'Stress rule', p. 183 (PDF pp. 6-7)
sources.note: Same author's published phonology summary states plain word-initial stress with no diphthong override (and transcribes ['nõmboil] with initial stress); worth citing alongside the thesis as corroboration of the initial default and as evidence that the CVV clause is the thesis's hedged addition.
